name: hypertension in pregnancy overview
title: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: chronic and gestational hypertension, split by onset before or after 20 weeks, where the blood pressure is the problem and is treated with oral drugs, against pre-eclampsia, eclampsia and HELLP syndrome, where it is a symptom, severe pressure is lowered with intravenous drugs, magnesium sulfate prevents seizures and complications decide delivery

root.title: High blood pressure (BP) in pregnancy: WHEN did it start, and is the BP the PROBLEM or a SYMPTOM?
lines: MILD: systolic > 140 or diastolic > 90 · SEVERE: systolic > 160 or diastolic > 110 · each on 2 readings > 15 min apart

groups.title: BP IS THE PROBLEM: treat the BP
BP IS A SYMPTOM: protect mother and fetus
lines: SEVERE BP risks STROKE: lower it urgently to < 160 / < 110
complications (their presence and severity) decide DELIVERY

head: h
Gestational hypertension
after 20 weeks
dx: NORMAL BPs documented up to 20 weeks
NO adverse conditions or severe complications
tx: angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers: fetal kidney failure, oligohydramnios

head: h
Pre-eclampsia
hypertension + PROTEINURIA
late gestation · more often a first pregnancy
dx: headache, visual change · chest pain, saturation < 97%
right upper quadrant pain · ↑ creatinine, liver enzymes
watch: acute kidney injury · international normalized ratio (INR) > 2 · abruption
tx: labetalol 20 mg IV, then 20–80 mg every 30 min (max 300 mg)
hydralazine 5 mg IV, then 5–10 mg every 30 min
once decided in SEVERE pre-eclampsia: MgSO4 →

head: h
Eclampsia
pre-eclampsia + SEIZURES
usually poorly controlled pre-eclampsia
watch: investigate: rule out an intracranial event
tx: load 4 g IV over 20 min, then 1–2 g/h

head: h
HELLP syndrome
Hemolysis · Elevated Liver enzymes · Low Platelets
atypical pre-eclampsia / eclampsia
